response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.cnt * 1.0) AS avg_count_above_average, AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_overall_average FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: The invoiced activity is the number of invoices (rows after the inner joins Invoices -> Orders -> Customers) per gender; NULL gender forms its own group via GROUP BY, and gender values are used as stored (no case normalization).
If no group's count is strictly above the average (e.g., all counts equal), the query returns one row with NULL values.
